steps.title: Self-service: top up stock
steps.prompt:
UPDATE rewrites values in EXISTING rows - like topping up the honey jar.
SET stock = stock + 10 says 'the new stock is the old stock plus ten'.
steps.task: Try typing: UPDATE products SET stock = stock + 10 WHERE id = 1;
hints: SET names the column to change.
stock + 10 adds ten to the old value.
Write: UPDATE products SET stock = stock + 10 WHERE id = 1;
steps.expected_sql: UPDATE products SET stock = stock + 10 WHERE id = 1;

steps.title: A 10% price rise
steps.prompt:
Sometimes a whole category gets a price rise.
UPDATE … SET price = price * 1.1 … hits every matching row at once.
steps.task: Try typing: UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1 WHERE category_id = 5;
hints: Write: UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1 WHERE category_id = 5;
steps.expected_sql: UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1 WHERE category_id = 5;
steps.memory_trick: One UPDATE, many rows - the WHERE decides how many.

steps.title: Fix one price
steps.prompt:
One product has a wrong price. Fill the SET clause:
UPDATE products SET ___ WHERE id = 2;
steps.task: Set the price of product id 2 to 24.99.
steps.expected_sql: UPDATE products SET price = 24.99 WHERE id = 2;
steps.memory_trick: SET column = new value - that's the whole medicine.

steps.title: Predict the forgetful UPDATE
steps.prompt:
If someone writes UPDATE products SET stock = 0; (no WHERE at all)…
What happens to the 40 rows?
steps.task: How many products end up with zero stock?
hints: The UPDATE touches every row it can.
steps.memory_trick: No WHERE = every row. That's why safety warnings exist.

steps.title: The safety habit
steps.prompt:
You'll see a friendly warning before UPDATE/DELETE that touches many rows.
It's not a scolding - it's a check-in, because the practice shop is YOURS to test.
Reset (the ↺ button) always brings everything back.
steps.task: What does the ↺ Reset button do?
hints: Look at the little arrow button near the output.
It looks like the redo/refresh symbol.
It brings back the shop you started with.
